summary: Shows the debugging run with ANSIBLE_KEEP_REMOTE_FILES and -vvv, then navigating to the temp directory and running the AnsiballZ wrapper's explode command to unpack the module into a debug_dir.
questions: How do I unpack the AnsiballZ wrapper to look at the real module code?
Where does Ansible put the temporary module file on the target?
What does the explode subcommand do?

answer_card.title: Explode an AnsiballZ module
answer_card.answer_md:
```shell-session
$ ANSIBLE_KEEP_REMOTE_FILES=1 ansible localhost -m ping -a 'data=debugging_session' -vvv
```
The output shows a path like `~/.ansible/tmp/ansible-tmp-.../AnsiballZ_ping.py`. Then:
```shell-session
$ ssh remotehost   # only for remote targets
$ cd ~/.ansible/tmp/ansible-tmp-...
$ python AnsiballZ_ping.py explode
```
This expands the base64 payload into a `debug_dir` of Python files.
